title: Building BIDS Apps with niflowr and bidsappr
text: bidsappr package lets build containerized BIDS Apps R zero boilerplate. niflowr provides neuroimaging operations wrappers FSL, ANTs, FreeSurfer, AFNI. Together, can build standards-compliant BIDS App wraps combination neuroimaging tools. BIDS App containerized neuroimaging pipeline follows BIDS Apps specification. accepts BIDS dataset input, runs participant-level /group-level analysis, writes outputs structured format.

title: Building BIDS Apps with niflowr and bidsappr
text: Scaffold new BIDS App single function call: creates: - app.R template participant/group functions - Dockerfile neuroimaging tools pre-installed - DESCRIPTION dependency metadata - Example configuration
code: library(niflowr)  ni_bids_app("~/my_brain_app", tools = c("fsl.bet", "fsl.flirt"))

title: Building BIDS Apps with niflowr and bidsappr
text: generated app.R defines two functions: participant() subject-level processing group() group-level analysis. ctx object provided bidsappr handles BIDS input/output conventions.
code: participant <- function(ctx, frac = 0.5) {   # ctx provides:   # - ctx$subject: current subject ID   # - ctx$files: list of input files for this subject   # - ctx$out_file(): function to create output paths   # - ctx$write_tsv(): function to write QC metrics    for (subj in ctx$subjects) {     t1w <- ctx$files[[subj]]$anat$T1w[[1]]      # Run niflowr operation     result <- ni_fsl_bet(       in_file = t1w,       out_file = ctx$out_file(subj, "brain.nii.gz"),       frac = frac,       .engine = "native"     )      # Log QC metrics     ctx$write_tsv(       subject = subj,       out_size = file.size(result$out_file),       exit_code = result$exit_code     )   } }  group <- function(ctx) {   # Access participant-level outputs   # Run group statistics, generate reports, etc. }

title: Building BIDS Apps with niflowr and bidsappr
text: complete working example runs BET T1w images: Run command line:
code: library(niflowr) library(bidsappr)  participant <- function(ctx, frac = 0.5, robust = FALSE) {   qc_metrics <- list()    for (subj in ctx$subjects) {     # Find T1w image     t1w_files <- ctx$files[[subj]]$anat$T1w     if (length(t1w_files) == 0) {       warning("No T1w found for ", subj)       next     }      t1w <- t1w_files[[1]]     out_brain <- ctx$out_file(subj, "anat", "brain.nii.gz")     out_mask <- ctx$out_file(subj, "anat", "brain_mask.nii.gz")      # Run brain extraction     result <- ni_fsl_bet(       in_file = t1w,       out_file = out_brain,       frac = frac,       robust = robust,       mask = TRUE,       .engine = "native"     )      # Collect QC metrics     qc_metrics[[subj]] <- data.frame(       subject_id = subj,       input_size_mb = file.size(t1w) / 1e6,       output_size_mb = file.size(out_brain) / 1e6,       frac_param = frac,       exit_status = result$exit_code,       timestamp = Sys.time()     )   }    # Write QC report   qc_df <- do.call(rbind, qc_metrics)   ctx$write_tsv(qc_df, "bet_qc.tsv") }  # Run the app if (!interactive()) {   bidsappr::main(app_dir = "my_brain_app") } Rscript app.R /data/bids /data/output participant --frac 0.3 --robust

title: Building BIDS Apps with niflowr and bidsappr
text: complex app chains multiple operations:
code: participant <- function(ctx, template = "MNI152_T1_2mm.nii.gz") {   for (subj in ctx$subjects) {     t1w <- ctx$files[[subj]]$anat$T1w[[1]]      # Step 1: Skull strip     brain <- ctx$out_file(subj, "anat", "brain.nii.gz")     ni_fsl_bet(       in_file = t1w,       out_file = brain,       frac = 0.5,       .engine = "native"     )      # Step 2: Register to template     mat_file <- ctx$out_file(subj, "anat", "brain_to_mni.mat")     reg_result <- ni_fsl_flirt(       in_file = brain,       ref = template,       out = ctx$out_file(subj, "anat", "brain_mni.nii.gz"),       omat = mat_file,       .engine = "native"     )      # Step 3: Apply transformation to original T1w     ni_fsl_flirt(       in_file = t1w,       ref = template,       init = mat_file,       applyxfm = TRUE,       out = ctx$out_file(subj, "anat", "T1w_mni.nii.gz"),       .engine = "native"     )      # Log pipeline completion     ctx$write_tsv(       subject = subj,       pipeline_complete = TRUE,       registration_exit = reg_result$exit_code     )   } }

title: Building BIDS Apps with niflowr and bidsappr
text: bidsappr scaffolds Dockerfile : - Installs R required packages - Pre-installs neuroimaging tools (FSL, ANTs, etc.) - Configures BIDS App entrypoint Build run: Inside container, use .engine = "native" since tools installed container image.
code: FROM rocker/r-ver:4.3.0  # Install neuroimaging tools RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \     fsl-core \     ants  # Install R packages RUN R -e "install.packages(c('niflowr', 'bidsappr'))"  # Copy app COPY app.R /app/ WORKDIR /app  ENTRYPOINT ["Rscript", "app.R"] docker build -t myapp . docker run myapp /bids /output participant --frac 0.3

title: Building BIDS Apps with niflowr and bidsappr
text: bidsappr automatically generates CLI flags function signatures. Function parameters become command-line options: Users can run: makes niflowr pipelines instantly accessible command-line tools without manual argument parsing.
code: participant <- function(ctx, frac = 0.5, robust = FALSE, threshold = 0.1) {   # frac, robust, threshold are now CLI parameters } Rscript app.R /bids /output participant \   --frac 0.3 \   --robust \   --threshold 0.05

title: Extending niflowr: wrap a new tool
text: Every wrapper niflowr built three artefacts: spec source truth. Wrappers golden command-line fixtures regenerated . Profiles kept separate spec can run natively CI, Docker container laptop, Apptainer cluster — without changes spec .

title: Extending niflowr: wrap a new tool
text: Let’s wrap mri_synthstrip bare minimum: input volume brain-mask output. ’ll write spec tempfile vignette can run end--end without touching package source. Now load build call: ’s . spec file plus ni_spec_read() plus ni_call() enough render safe, validated command-line vector. shell strings, paste0 — niflowr keeps command arguments separate can never collide shell metacharacters. dry_run confirms wiring without invoking binary:
code: spec_path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json") writeLines(c(   '{',   '  "spec_version": "0.1.0",',   '  "id": "demo.synthstrip",',   '  "title": "SynthStrip (demo)",',   '  "command": "mri_synthstrip",',   '  "inputs": {',   '    "in_file":   {"type": "file", "required": true,',   '                  "cli": {"argstr": "-i %s"}},',   '    "mask_file": {"type": "file",',   '                  "cli": {"argstr": "-m %s"}}',   '  },',   '  "outputs": {',   '    "mask_file": {"type": "file",',   '                  "path": {"from_input": "mask_file"},',   '                  "must_exist": false}',   '  },',   '  "runtime": {"profile": "freesurfer"}',   '}' ), spec_path) spec <- ni_spec_read(spec_path)  call <- ni_call(spec,   in_file   = system.file("DESCRIPTION", package = "niflowr"),   mask_file = "/tmp/T1_mask.nii.gz",   .engine   = "native" )  ni_cmd(call) #> $command #> [1] "mri_synthstrip" #>  #> $args #> [1] "-i"                                                  #> [2] "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/niflowr/DESCRIPTION" #> [3] "-m"                                                  #> [4] "/tmp/T1_mask.nii.gz"                                 #>  #> $wd #> NULL #>  #> $env #> NULL #>  #> $engine #> [1] "native" #>  #> $profile #> NULL #>  #> $stdout #> NULL #>  #> $stderr #> NULL ni_run(call, dry_run = TRUE, echo = FALSE)

title: Extending niflowr: wrap a new tool
text: minimal spec hides moving parts. input definition can carry: four blocks matter: type — one file, dir, string, int, double, bool, flag, enum, list. Drives R coercion wrapper’s @param documentation. validate — fail fast ni_call()-time. exists (file/dir must present), min/max (numeric range), regex (string pattern). Errors surface clean cli::cli_abort() messages instead mysterious crashes inside binary. cli.argstr — printf-style format string. %s files / strings, %d ints, %.2f etc. doubles. Flags use literal switch like -g (%). constraints — xor (mutually exclusive) requires (co-required). Validated call time.
code: "frac": {   "type": "double",   "desc": "Fractional intensity threshold",   "default": 0.5,   "validate": {"min": 0, "max": 1},   "cli": {"argstr": "-f %.2f"},   "constraints": {"xor": ["robust"]} }

title: Extending niflowr: wrap a new tool
text: CLIs mix two. niflowr handles shape: position orders positional args (negative values count end — useful trailing arguments like mri_watershed .mgz .mgz). Switched arguments render alphabetical order positionals, shape deterministic golden-testable.
code: "in_file":  {"type": "file", "required": true,              "cli": {"argstr": "%s", "position": 0}}, "out_file": {"type": "file",              "cli": {"argstr": "%s", "position": 1}}, "frac":     {"type": "double",              "cli": {"argstr": "-f %.2f"}}

title: Extending niflowr: wrap a new tool
text: Working tempfile fine one-experiments. ship wrapper part package (fork niflowr, downstream package depends ), promote spec package development loop: 1. Drop spec inst/specs/. Naming convention <profile>.<tool>.json, spec id matching filename: 2. Lint . catches shell metacharacters, positional collisions, malformed flags, constraint references point inputs don’t exist: fix = TRUE mode linter rewrites safe cases place (> %s → stdout_to, dropped duplicate positions, normalised constraint arrays). 3. Regenerate wrapper. produces R/wrappers_auto.R specs inst/specs/ — new one existing 300+: wrapper named ni_freesurfer_synthstrip() now exists, one @param per input dry_run / echo / .cwd / .engine / .profile controls. 4. Update NAMESPACE man pages. 5. Refresh golden command-line fixture. regression test protects accidental CLI changes — every spec gets deterministic input/output snapshot: 6. Write test. Mirror pattern tests/testthat/test-fastsurfer.R tests/testthat/test-freesurfer-synthstrip.R: load spec, build call synthetic temp files, assert rendered cmd$args, finish dry_run smoke test. ’s entire loop. bundled inst/specs/freesurfer.synthstrip.json full version example built — 70 lines, covering -, -o, -m, -d, -b, -g, -t, ---csf, --model. Read next vignette see moving parts natural habitat.
code: inst/specs/freesurfer.synthstrip.json ni_lint_specs(strict = TRUE) Rscript tools/gen_wrappers.R Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise(".")' Rscript tools/gen_golden_cmdline.R test_that("freesurfer.synthstrip renders core CLI args", {   in_file <- withr::local_tempfile(fileext = ".nii.gz")   file.create(in_file)   call <- ni_call("freesurfer.synthstrip",     in_file = in_file,     mask_file = "/tmp/mask.nii.gz",     gpu = TRUE   )   cmd <- ni_cmd(call)   expect_equal(cmd$command, "mri_synthstrip")   expect_true(all(c("-i", in_file) %in% cmd$args))   expect_true(all(c("-m", "/tmp/mask.nii.gz") %in% cmd$args))   expect_true("-g" %in% cmd$args) })

title: Extending niflowr: wrap a new tool
text: things linter catch easier get right first time: Don’t put % placeholders flag types. flag presence / absence — argstr literal switch (-g, -g %s). Don’t redirect shell metacharacters. "argstr": "> %s" illegal niflowr never invokes shell. Use cli.stdout_to: "out_file" instead — runner handles redirection . Don’t use position two required inputs. Use distinct integers, negative positions trailing args. Validate boundary. Numeric ranges, regex patterns, exists: true far cheaper half-completed run crashes inside binary.

Existing specs inst/specs/ best reference. fsl.bet.json shows xor constraints anger; fastsurfer.run.json shows template output paths; freesurfer.synthmorph_register.json shows trailing positionals via negative position. title: From fMRIPrep to post-processing with niflowr
text: fmriprepper package orchestrates fMRIPrep execution — builds commands, handles batch submission, integrates HPC schedulers. niflowr package handles post-fMRIPrep processing — additional skull stripping, registration custom templates, ROI extraction, building reproducible pipelines targets. vignette shows chain together complete preprocessing analysis workflow.

title: From fMRIPrep to post-processing with niflowr
code: Raw BIDS data     ↓ fmriprepper (orchestrate fMRIPrep)     ↓ fMRIPrep derivatives (preprocessed data)     ↓ niflowr (post-processing)     ↓ Final results

title: From fMRIPrep to post-processing with niflowr

code: library(fmriprepper)  plan <- fmriprep()$   bids("/data/bids")$   out("/data/derivatives")$   engine_singularity(image = "/images/fmriprep.sif")$   participant_labels(c("01", "02", "03"))$   nprocs(16)$   omp_nthreads(8)$   spaces_all()  # Run locally (or use plan$write_slurm_array("submit.sbatch") for HPC) plan$run()

Handle missing subjects: subjects may complete successfully. Use ni_fmriprep_derivatives() discover subjects valid outputs, filter subject list accordingly. HPC considerations: large datasets, use fmriprepper’s SLURM array integration (write_slurm_array()) parallelize fMRIPrep across subjects. derivatives ready, use targets parallel backend (tar_make_future()) scale niflowr post-processing. Version tracking: packages write provenance metadata. Check dataset_description.json fMRIPrep derivatives niflowr’s container runtime metadata ensure reproducibility.

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Neuroimaging pipelines call many command-line tools — FSL’s bet, ANTs’ antsRegistration, FreeSurfer’s recon-— argument syntax, validation quirks, output conventions. Wrapping R typically means writing brittle system() calls paste()-assembled shell strings, input validation, record ran. niflowr takes different approach: Tool interfaces defined JSON specs, executable code. spec declares inputs, outputs, CLI rendering rules, validation constraints. Commands built argument vectors, never shell strings — quoting bugs, injection hazards. Execution captures provenance — command ran, arguments, long took, produced. Pipeline orchestration left {targets} — niflowr handles interface layer; {targets} {crew} handle scheduling, caching, parallelism.

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: ’s looks like run FSL’s brain extraction tool: single call validated inputs, built safe argument vector, ran bet via processx, checked outputs exist, wrote provenance sidecar — without single paste() system().

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: niflowr three core objects flow : ni_spec — tool interface definition (JSON) ni_call — spec bound concrete parameter values ni_result — execution output runtime info provenance

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: ni_call() binds parameter values spec. validates inputs immediately — required parameters, file existence, numeric ranges, mutual exclusion constraints: inputs valid, get back call object can inspect:
code: # This fails: frac must be between 0 and 1 ni_call("fsl.bet",   in_file  = "/tmp/t1.nii.gz",   out_file = "/tmp/brain.nii.gz",   frac     = 1.5,   .validate = FALSE  # skip file-exists check for this demo ) #>  #> ── ni_call: fsl.bet #> Command: `bet /tmp/t1.nii.gz /tmp/brain.nii.gz -f 1.50` #>  #> ── Expected outputs #> out_file: /tmp/brain.nii.gz call <- ni_call("fsl.bet",   in_file  = "/tmp/t1.nii.gz",   out_file = "/tmp/brain.nii.gz",   frac     = 0.3,   mask     = TRUE,   .validate = FALSE ) call #>  #> ── ni_call: fsl.bet #> Command: `bet /tmp/t1.nii.gz /tmp/brain.nii.gz -f 0.30 -m` #>  #> ── Expected outputs #> out_file: /tmp/brain.nii.gz

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: running anything, can see exactly command executed. niflowr never hides ’s : args vector gets passed processx::run() — element separate argument, never concatenated shell string.
code: ni_cmd(call) #> $command #> [1] "bet" #>  #> $args #> [1] "/tmp/t1.nii.gz"    "/tmp/brain.nii.gz" "-f"                #> [4] "0.30"              "-m"                #>  #> $wd #> NULL #>  #> $env #> NULL #>  #> $engine #> NULL #>  #> $profile #> NULL #>  #> $stdout #> NULL #>  #> $stderr #> NULL

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: ni_run() runs command returns ni_result:
code: result <- ni_run(call) result #> -- ni_result: fsl.bet [success] -- #> Exit status: 0 #> Duration: 12.3s #> #> -- Outputs -- #>   out_file: /tmp/brain.nii.gz #>   mask_file: /tmp/brain.nii.gz_mask.nii.gz

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: just want preview command without executing , use dry_run = TRUE shorthand ni_dry_run():
code: ni_dry_run("fsl.bet",   in_file  = "/tmp/t1.nii.gz",   out_file = "/tmp/brain.nii.gz",   frac     = 0.5,   .engine  = "native" ) #> ℹ Dry run [native]: `bet /tmp/t1.nii.gz /tmp/brain.nii.gz -f 0.50` #>  #> ── Expected outputs #> out_file: /tmp/brain.nii.gz

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Every bundled spec corresponding wrapper function typed arguments documentation. recommended way call tools: wrapper calls ni_call() + ni_run() internally, get validation, safe execution, provenance:
code: # Linear registration with FLIRT result <- ni_fsl_flirt(   in_file         = "func_mean.nii.gz",   reference       = "MNI152_T1_2mm.nii.gz",   out_file        = "func_mean_mni.nii.gz",   out_matrix_file = "func2mni.mat",   dof             = 12,   cost            = "corratio" )

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Every successful run writes JSON sidecar next primary output. records exact command, arguments, timing, (optionally) input file hashes:
code: # After running bet... prov <- ni_provenance(result) prov$command #> [1] "bet" prov$args #> [1] "/data/sub-01_T1w.nii.gz" "/data/sub-01_brain.nii.gz" "-f" "0.5" "-m" prov$duration_secs #> [1] 12.3  # Or read a sidecar from disk ni_provenance_read("sub-01_brain_provenance.json")

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: niflowr can run tools inside Docker Apptainer containers. Container execution profile-driven via niflowr.yml, stable container paths (/, /, /work): Wrappers always accept host paths; path mapping container paths handled inside ni_run().
code: # Configure once per project (or rely on automatic niflowr.yml discovery): ni_config(config_file = "niflowr.yml")  result <- ni_fsl_bet(   in_file    = "/data/t1.nii.gz",   out_file   = "/data/brain.nii.gz",   .engine    = "auto",   # native first, then container fallback by runtime.prefer   .profile   = "fsl"     # maps to profiles.fsl in niflowr.yml ) # Runs natively if `bet` exists; otherwise uses configured container backend.

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: niflowr includes specs FastSurfer, GPU-accelerated alternative FreeSurfer runs brain segmentation ~5 minutes. FastSurfer runs primarily via container, configure profile niflowr.yml: call wrapper:
code: profiles:   fastsurfer:     docker_image: "deepmi/fastsurfer:cpu-v2.4.2"     apptainer_uri: "docker://deepmi/fastsurfer:cpu-v2.4.2" # Full pipeline: segmentation + surface reconstruction result <- ni_fastsurfer_run(   t1     = "sub-01_T1w.nii.gz",   sid    = "sub-01",   sd     = "derivatives/fastsurfer",   device = "cuda",   .engine = "docker" )  # Segmentation only (~5 min) seg <- ni_fastsurfer_segment(   t1     = "sub-01_T1w.nii.gz",   sid    = "sub-01",   sd     = "derivatives/fastsurfer",   device = "cpu" ) ni_outputs(seg) #> $seg_file #> [1] "derivatives/fastsurfer/sub-01/mri/aparc.DKTatlas+aseg.deep.mgz" #> $mask_file #> [1] "derivatives/fastsurfer/sub-01/mri/mask.mgz"

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Use ni_doctor() check runtime binaries, mounted roots, profile definitions, lockfile consistency:
code: report <- ni_doctor() report  # Strict mode errors on failures: ni_doctor(strict = TRUE)

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Use ni_pin() create/update lockfile resolved runtime references configured profiles, ni_lock_validate() verify current config matches lock:
code: # Create/update lockfile (default: runtime.lockfile or niflowr.lock.yml) lock <- ni_pin()  # Validate current config against lockfile checks <- ni_lock_validate() checks

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Enable lock enforcement ensure containerized runs use lockfile-pinned references:
code: ni_config(config = list(   runtime = list(     lockfile = "niflowr.lock.yml",     lock_enforce = TRUE   ) ))  # When lock_enforce = TRUE, ni_run() resolves container refs from the lockfile # for the selected profile and errors if lock constraints are violated. result <- ni_fsl_bet(   in_file  = "/data/t1.nii.gz",   out_file = "/data/brain.nii.gz",   .engine  = "docker",   .profile = "fsl" )

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: niflowr designed work three companion packages:

what: neuroim2 — read outputs as R objects
title: Getting started with niflowr
text: running tool, load output directly neuroim2 NeuroVol NeuroVec:
code: result <- ni_fsl_bet(in_file = "t1.nii.gz", out_file = "brain.nii.gz") brain <- ni_read_output(result, "out_file") # Returns a NeuroVol — you can slice, plot, do math on it

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Registration outputs can loaded neurotransform morphism objects composition resampling:
code: reg <- ni_fsl_flirt(   in_file = "func.nii.gz", reference = "t1.nii.gz",   out_file = "func_t1.nii.gz", out_matrix_file = "func2t1.mat" ) xfm <- ni_read_transform(reg, "out_matrix_file") # Returns an Affine3DMorphism — compose, invert, resample with it

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Query BIDS dataset inputs generate derivatives-style output paths:
code: library(bidser) proj <- bids_project("/data/bids")  # Find T1w images for a subject inputs <- ni_bids_inputs(proj, "fsl.bet", subid = "01", modality = "T1w")  # Generate a BIDS-derivatives output path ni_deriv_path(inputs$path[1], desc = "brain", suffix = "T1w") #> [1] "derivatives/niflowr/sub-01/anat/sub-01_desc-brain_T1w.nii.gz"

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: multi-step pipelines, niflowr integrates {targets} DAG-based execution caching parallelism. key idea: niflowr handles interface layer, {targets} handles execution layer.

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: simplest pattern uses ni_run_files(), returns output paths suitable format = "file" targets:
code: # _targets.R library(targets) library(niflowr)  list(   tar_target(     brain,     ni_run_files("fsl.bet",       in_file  = "data/sub-01_T1w.nii.gz",       out_file = "derivatives/sub-01_desc-brain_T1w.nii.gz",       frac = 0.5     ),     format = "file"   ) )

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: tar_ni_step() target factory wraps pattern:
code: list(   tar_ni_step(brain, "fsl.bet",     in_file  = "data/sub-01_T1w.nii.gz",     out_file = "derivatives/sub-01_desc-brain_T1w.nii.gz",     frac = 0.5   ) )

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Process multiple subjects parallel {targets} dynamic branching {crew} workers: {targets} skips subjects whose outputs already date, {crew} distributes work across 8 parallel workers.
code: library(targets) library(crew) library(niflowr) library(bidser)  tar_option_set(   packages = c("niflowr", "bidser"),   controller = crew_controller_local(workers = 8) )  list(   tar_target(bids, bidser::bids_project("data/bids")),    tar_target(t1w_files,     bidser::search_files(bids, regex = "_T1w\\.nii", full_path = TRUE)   ),    tar_target(brain, {     out <- ni_deriv_path(t1w_files, desc = "brain")     ni_run_files("fsl.bet", in_file = t1w_files, out_file = out, frac = 0.5)   }, pattern = map(t1w_files), format = "file") )

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: can write specs command-line tool. vignette("extending-niflowr") vignette walks full loop (spec → lint → wrapper → golden → test) using SynthStrip worked example. short version: create JSON file following schema inst/schema/niflowr-spec-0.1.0.json: Load path:
code: {   "spec_version": "0.1.0",   "id": "my.tool",   "title": "My Custom Tool",   "command": "mytool",   "inputs": {     "in_file": {       "type": "file",       "required": true,       "validate": { "exists": true },       "cli": { "argstr": "--input %s" }     },     "threshold": {       "type": "double",       "validate": { "min": 0, "max": 1 },       "cli": { "argstr": "--thresh %g" }     }   },   "outputs": {     "out_file": {       "type": "file",       "path": { "template": "{in_file}_processed.nii.gz" },       "must_exist": true     }   } } spec <- ni_spec_read("/path/to/my.tool.json") result <- ni_run(ni_call(spec, in_file = "data.nii.gz", threshold = 0.5))

title: Getting started with niflowr
text: Browse bundled specs ni_spec_list() ni_spec_read() see real interfaces defined See ?ni_call full set validation constraint options See ?ni_run execution options (echo, provenance, container) See ?tar_ni_step {targets} integration details See ?ni_read_output ?ni_read_transform ecosystem helpers

title: From OpenNeuro to analysis with niflowr
text: vignette demonstrates end--end neuroimaging workflow R combining two packages: openneuroR: fetches BIDS datasets OpenNeuro niflowr: processes neuroimaging data FSL, AFNI, ANTs, tools Together, provide reproducible pipeline data acquisition analysis, entirely within R.

title: From OpenNeuro to analysis with niflowr
text: Install packages GitHub:
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("bbuchsbaum/openneuroR") pak::pak("bbuchsbaum/niflowr")  library(openneuroR) library(niflowr)

title: From OpenNeuro to analysis with niflowr
text: Use on_search() find datasets keyword, on_dataset() view metadata:
code: # Search for flanker task datasets results <- on_search("flanker")  # View details for ds000102 (flanker task) dataset <- on_dataset("ds000102") dataset$description

title: From OpenNeuro to analysis with niflowr
text: convenience function ni_from_openneuro() downloads dataset returns BIDS object: downloads ~/openneuro_data/ds000102/ default. Specify target_dir customize.
code: # Download first 3 subjects bids <- ni_from_openneuro("ds000102", subjects = c("01", "02", "03"))  # Inspect the BIDS structure print(bids)

title: From OpenNeuro to analysis with niflowr
text: Use ni_bids_inputs() find files matching specific modality, process :
code: # Find T1w images for subject 01 inputs <- ni_bids_inputs(bids, "fsl.bet", subid = "01", modality = "T1w")  # Skull strip with FSL BET result <- ni_fsl_bet(   in_file = inputs$path[1],   out_file = ni_deriv_path(inputs$path[1], desc = "brain"),   frac = 0.5 )

title: From OpenNeuro to analysis with niflowr
text: Chain operations using output one step input next:
code: # Register brain-extracted T1w to MNI152 reg_result <- ni_fsl_flirt(   in_file = result$out_file,   ref_file = ni_fsl_template("MNI152_T1_2mm_brain"),   out_file = ni_deriv_path(result$out_file, space = "MNI152"),   out_matrix_file = ni_deriv_path(result$out_file, suffix = "xfm", ext = "mat") )

title: From OpenNeuro to analysis with niflowr
text: Use targets process multiple subjects parallel: Run targets::tar_make().
code: library(targets)  # _targets.R tar_option_set(packages = c("niflowr", "openneuroR"))  list(   tar_target(bids, ni_from_openneuro("ds000102", subjects = c("01", "02", "03"))),    tar_target(     subjects,     bids$participants$participant_id   ),    tar_target(     brain_extracted,     {       inputs <- ni_bids_inputs(bids, "fsl.bet", subid = subjects, modality = "T1w")       ni_fsl_bet(         in_file = inputs$path[1],         out_file = ni_deriv_path(inputs$path[1], desc = "brain"),         frac = 0.5       )     },     pattern = map(subjects)   ),    tar_target(     registered,     {       ni_fsl_flirt(         in_file = brain_extracted$out_file,         ref_file = ni_fsl_template("MNI152_T1_2mm_brain"),         out_file = ni_deriv_path(brain_extracted$out_file, space = "MNI152")       )     },     pattern = map(brain_extracted)   ) )

title: From OpenNeuro to analysis with niflowr
text: dataset preprocessed derivatives OpenNeuro, download use directly:
code: # Download fMRIPrep derivatives on_download_derivatives(   dataset = "ds000102",   derivative = "fmriprep",   dest_dir = "~/openneuro_data/ds000102/derivatives",   subjects = c("01", "02") )  # Load confounds confounds <- ni_fmriprep_confounds(   "~/openneuro_data/ds000102/derivatives/fmriprep/sub-01/func/sub-01_task-flanker_desc-confounds_timeseries.tsv" )  # Load preprocessed BOLD preproc <- ni_fmriprep_preproc(   "~/openneuro_data/ds000102/derivatives/fmriprep/sub-01/func/sub-01_task-flanker_space-MNI152NLin2009cAsym_desc-preproc_bold.nii.gz" )

title: Spec-Driven Neuroimaging Command-Line Tool Wrappers
text: Spec-driven R wrappers neuroimaging command-line tools — validated command building, execution, provenance. niflowr gives typed, validated, provenance-tracked R functions 300+ commands across FSL, AFNI, ANTs, FreeSurfer, FastSurfer, dcm2niix — without writing single system() call. tool interface JSON specification, wrappers consistent, inspectable, easy extend. single call validated inputs, built safe argument vector (shell string), ran bet via processx, confirmed output exists, wrote provenance sidecar — paste() quoting bugs.
code: result <- ni_fsl_bet(   in_file  = "sub-01_T1w.nii.gz",   out_file = "sub-01_desc-brain_T1w.nii.gz",   frac     = 0.5,   mask     = TRUE )  ni_outputs(result) #> $out_file #> [1] "sub-01_desc-brain_T1w.nii.gz"

title: Spec-Driven Neuroimaging Command-Line Tool Wrappers
text: Neuroimaging pipelines stitch together dozens command-line tools, flag syntax, validation quirks, output-naming conventions. Wrapping R usually means brittle system() calls paste()-assembled shell strings: input checking, silent failures typo’d flag, shell-injection hazards, record actually ran.

title: Spec-Driven Neuroimaging Command-Line Tool Wrappers
text: Tools described, hand-wrapped. Every interface declarative JSON spec listing inputs, outputs, CLI-rendering rules, constraints. shared engine turns specs R functions. Commands argument vectors, never shell strings. Values go straight processx character vector, without shell interpolation word splitting. Inputs validated anything runs — required fields, types, enum choices, numeric ranges, cross-argument constraints (xor, requires). Runs carry provenance metadata. returned ni_result includes exact command, engine/container, outputs, exit status, timing; successful file-producing runs can also write JSON sidecar. Reproducibility hooks explicit. Run natively, Docker, Apptainer/Singularity; pin image digests lockfile need stricter execution record. Workflow orchestration stays outside niflowr. niflowr command-interface layer; targets (crew) handle scheduling, caching, parallelism.

code: library(niflowr)  ni_cmd(ni_call("fsl.bet",   in_file  = "sub-01_T1w.nii.gz",   out_file = "sub-01_desc-brain_T1w.nii.gz",   frac     = 0.5,   mask     = TRUE )) #> $command #> [1] "bet" #> $args #> [1] "sub-01_T1w.nii.gz" "sub-01_desc-brain_T1w.nii.gz" "-f" "0.50" "-m" #> ... ni_dry_run("fsl.bet",   in_file  = "/data/sub-01_T1w.nii.gz",   out_file = "/out/sub-01_brain.nii.gz",   frac     = 0.5 ) # Ergonomic, tab-completable wrapper res <- ni_fsl_bet(in_file = "T1w.nii.gz", out_file = "brain.nii.gz", frac = 0.5)  # Generic equivalent — handy for programmatic / metaprogrammed pipelines res <- ni_run(ni_call("fsl.bet",   in_file = "T1w.nii.gz", out_file = "brain.nii.gz", frac = 0.5 ))  ni_outputs(res)      # named list of produced files ni_provenance(res)   # full record of what ran ni_fsl_bet(in_file = "T1w.nii.gz", out_file = "brain.nii.gz") |>   ni_fsl_flirt(reference = "MNI152.nii.gz", out_file = "brain_mni.nii.gz")

title: Spec-Driven Neuroimaging Command-Line Tool Wrappers

Inputs checked execution spec — types, required fields, enum choices, numeric min/max, regex patterns, relational constraints (xor, requires). bad call fails loudly R instead producing cryptic tool error (worse, silently wrong output).

title: Spec-Driven Neuroimaging Command-Line Tool Wrappers
text: ni_run() returns ni_result, result includes provenance metadata execution. Failed commands can returned setting error_on_status = FALSE; otherwise raise error. provenance = TRUE (default), command exits successfully, spec least one declared output, niflowr also writes *_provenance.json sidecar next primary output. sidecar captures spec id, full command argument vector, execution engine/profile, input-file checksums (xxhash64), output paths, exit status, timing. Read back anytime:
code: ni_provenance_read("sub-01_desc-brain_T1w.nii.gz_provenance.json")
